We propose a regularized proximal-extragradient algorithm in which both the forward and backward steps are performed with respect to dynamically regularized operators and functions, respectively. Under geometric assumptions on the inner problem analogous to those in the smooth setting, we establish last-iterate convergence rates for both the outer and inner residuals, together with weak convergence of the iterates to optimal solutions of the bilevel problem.
tldr: This paper develops regularized extragradient methods for bilevel optimization problems in Hilbert spaces, proving last-iterate convergence rates under geometric conditions.
motivation: Bilevel optimization problems are challenging and arise in various applications; the aim is to design efficient algorithms with theoretical guarantees for both continuous and discrete time settings.
method: The authors propose a first-order dynamical system and a proximal-extragradient algorithm, both incorporating dynamic regularization, and analyze their convergence under Attouch-Czarnecki-type conditions or sharpness.
result: They establish last-iterate convergence rates for outer and inner residuals and weak convergence of trajectories/iterates to optimal solutions in both smooth and nonsmooth settings.
conclusion: The paper contributes to optimization theory by providing novel convergence guarantees for bilevel problems, but it is unrelated to the specified research interests in quantum information and related areas.

title: Risk-averse Design Optimization With CVaR Constraints Via Multifidelity Tail-region Correction
authors: Dongjin Lee Gyeolhee Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Risk-averse design optimization with conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraints requires accurate tail estimates, but repeated high-fidelity (HF) evaluations are costly. We propose a multifidelity (MF) tail-region correction method that uses dimensionally decomposed generalized polynomial chaos expansion (DD-GPCE) as a global surrogate and directs a limited HF budget to responses that most strongly influence CVaR. Covariance of the estimated DD-GPCE coefficients quantifies finite-sample prediction uncertainty and defines a confidence-interval-based tail region. Within this region, a two-stage strategy explores locations with high prediction uncertainty and then exploits locations with large correction-induced shifts. A Tikhonov-regularized residual expansion using the same polynomial basis yields a unified tail-corrected surrogate. For a ten-bar truss, the method produced a design close to the crude-MCS reference with approximately 72 to 274 times fewer HF evaluations than the considered MF importance sampling configurations. For a suction valve, it reduced mass by 1.05% and bending and bulging CVaR by 17.68% and 21.53%, respectively, while satisfying the valve-opening requirement. The results demonstrate accurate, HF-sample-efficient CVaR-constrained design through localized MF correction.
tldr: This paper presents a multifidelity tail-region correction method for risk-averse design optimization with CVaR constraints, reducing high-fidelity evaluations significantly.
motivation: Risk-averse design optimization with CVaR constraints requires accurate tail estimates, but repeated high-fidelity evaluations are costly.
method: It uses dimensionally decomposed generalized polynomial chaos expansion (DD-GPCE) as a global surrogate and directs a limited high-fidelity budget to responses that most influence CVaR, with a two-stage strategy for tail region exploration and exploitation.
result: For a ten-bar truss, it needed 72-274 times fewer high-fidelity evaluations than MF importance sampling; for a suction valve, it reduced mass by 1.05% and CVaR by ~17-21% while satisfying constraints.
conclusion: The method achieves accurate, high-fidelity-sample-efficient CVaR-constrained design through localized multifidelity correction.

title: Entropy-Stable And Physical-Constraint-Preserving Dgsem For Symmetry-Reduced General-Relativistic Hydrodynamics On Stationary Spacetimes
authors: Jian-Guo Liu Guosheng Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an entropy-stable and physical-constraint-preserving discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method for symmetry-reduced general-relativistic hydrodynamics on prescribed stationary spacetimes. Using a local orthonormal transformation, the fluid variables are expressed in a form for which the relativistic hydrodynamic algebra and the admissible set are independent of the spatial metric, while the spacetime geometry enters through stationary coefficients. This separation allows entropy-conservative special-relativistic fluxes to be combined with a compatible discretization of the geometric source terms. On affine tensor-product meshes, the resulting DGSEM is conservative and satisfies a semidiscrete entropy inequality, while the transformed variables provide a convex framework for physical-constraint preservation. For practical stabilization, we use a geometry-only causal speed that is sufficient for both classical local Lax--Friedrichs entropy dissipation and the physical-constraint-preserving Lax--Friedrichs splitting. The fully discrete method combines this stabilization with SSP Runge--Kutta time stepping, oscillation elimination, and conservative local-orthonormal-state scaling. Numerical experiments cover smooth and strongly shocked special-relativistic flows, an axisymmetric jet, stationary Michel accretion, Schwarzschild Bondi--Hoyle flow, and four Kerr accretion cases. The results demonstrate the designed high-order accuracy in smooth regimes and robust performance for demanding relativistic flows on curved stationary backgrounds.
tldr: Develops an entropy-stable and physical-constraint-preserving discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method for symmetry-reduced general-relativistic hydrodynamics on stationary spacetimes.
motivation: To design high-order accurate numerical schemes that ensure entropy stability and physical constraints for relativistic flows on curved backgrounds.
method: Uses a local orthonormal transformation, entropy-conservative fluxes, a geometry-only causal speed for stabilization, and SSP Runge-Kutta time stepping.
result: Demonstrates designed high-order accuracy in smooth regimes and robust performance for shocked flows, jet, and accretion cases.
conclusion: The method provides a robust and accurate framework for simulating relativistic hydrodynamics on stationary spacetimes.

title: Nechvile-Transformed Spacecraft Dynamics And Propellant Computation In The 3-Body Problem
authors: Isaac M. Ross Michael J. Dixon
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The uncontrolled equations of motion in the Nechvile frame for the restricted three-body problem have been well-known since at least the 1960s. It would seem that adding an external force to these equations is quite trivial: simply add an external force per mass term to the acceleration equations. Here we show that the last statement is not true. In fact, we show that the additive generic external force must be multiplied by the inverse of [MATH] where [MATH] is the relative eccentricity of the primaries and [MATH] is the true anomaly of the rotating frame located at the barycenter. Furthermore, when this result is combined with the mass flow rate equation, it generates several surprising results due to the mismatch between the resulting quadratic term and the cubic term in the equations of motion. This leads to a corresponding modification of the rocket equation itself. A Birkhoff-theoretic solution to an illustrative cislunar space mission problem shows propellent savings of 80% with the use of the correct cost functional. The popular quadratic cost utilizes more than [MATH] the minimum propellant consumption.
tldr: This paper derives a corrected external force term for the Nechvile-transformed restricted three-body problem, leading to a revised rocket equation and large propellant savings in cislunar missions when using the proper cost functional.
motivation: The uncontrolled Nechvile-frame equations are well-known, but adding external forces naively is incorrect; the correct transformation requires scaling by the inverse of relative eccentricity and true anomaly, affecting spacecraft dynamics and propellant calculations.
method: The authors analytically derive the correct form of the external force in the Nechvile frame and combine it with mass flow rate equations, then apply a Birkhoff-theoretic approach to solve an illustrative cislunar mission problem comparing cost functionals.
result: The corrected cost functional yields 80% propellant savings compared to the popular quadratic cost, which overestimates consumption by more than a factor related to the mismatch between quadratic and cubic terms.
conclusion: The research is purely in classical astrodynamics and mission design, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems, and is thus outside the user's research scope.

title: Value Of Information In Dynamic Decision Making
authors: Eilon Solan Dimitry Shaiderman
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the value of information in predicting the evolving state of a finite Markov chain. At each stage, a decision maker chooses a state and observes only whether the current state of the chain matches her choice; the resulting information is used to make a prediction on the state at the final stage of the problem. We show that, when the chain starts from an invariant distribution, the optimal terminal value is non-decreasing with the number of observations and converges at a uniform exponential rate. We introduce the predictive learning index, which measures whether all attainable informational value is extracted after finitely many observations, and show that both finite and infinite indices may occur. In contrast, for nonstationary initial distributions, the value may strictly decrease with the horizon.
tldr: This paper studies the value of information in a dynamic decision problem for predicting a Markov chain, showing convergence results and introducing a learning index, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how partial observations can be optimally used to predict the future state of a stochastic process, and to quantify the value of information in a sequential decision-making setting.
method: Formulates a dynamic programming problem where the decision maker chooses states to observe partial matches, and analyzes the optimal terminal value as a function of the number of observations.
result: For invariant initial distributions, the optimal value is non-decreasing and converges exponentially; a predictive learning index is introduced to classify when all information is extracted after finite observations. For nonstationary distributions, the value can decrease with horizon.
conclusion: The value of information in such problems has a rich structure, but the setting is classical and does not connect to the specified quantum information research directions.

title: Numerical Range And Invariant Subspaces Of Weighted Composition Operators On The Hardy Space Of Dirichlet Series
authors: Sudeshna Lahiri, Sarita Ojha, Subhadip Halder, Riddhick Birbonshi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study various results on numerical range of weighted composition operators on Hardy space of Dirichlet series. Certain conditions are provided under which the numerical range contains zero and some circular or elliptic disks. With the help of invariant subspaces of the operator, we also determine the numerical range of reductive weighted composition operators on this space. Additionally, we discuss some results on the Davis-Wielandt shell of composition operators with some natural questions that arise from our findings.
tldr: This paper studies numerical ranges of weighted composition operators on the Hardy space of Dirichlet series, providing conditions for containment of zero and disks, and determining ranges for reductive operators via invariant subspaces.
motivation: To advance operator theory by investigating properties of weighted composition operators on this specific function space.
method: The authors use invariant subspaces and structural properties of the operators to derive conditions on the numerical range and study the Davis-Wielandt shell.
result: They establish conditions under which the numerical range contains zero or circular/elliptic disks, and explicitly describe the range for reductive operators.
conclusion: The work contributes to functional analysis but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information or related fields.

title: Mohsen Hachtroudi And The Geometry Of Differential Equations
authors: Masoud Khalkhali
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mohsen Hachtroudi (1908--1976) was one of the founders of modern mathematics in Iran and the first Iranian mathematician to gain international recognition for original research in modern times. A student of \'Elie Cartan, he introduced the canonical projective connection now known as the , whose significance has become increasingly apparent through later developments in Cartan geometry, CR geometry, and parabolic geometry. This article combines a historical and mathematical study of\\ Hachtroudi's life and work. It examines his education in Iran and France, his role in establishing modern mathematical research and higher education in Iran, and his influence as a teacher, essayist, and public intellectual. It also presents a modern account of his mathematical contributions and their continuing impact on the geometry of differential equations and the theory of geometric structures.
tldr: A historical and mathematical account of Mohsen Hachtroudi's life and his contributions to the geometry of differential equations, particularly the canonical projective connection.
motivation: To document the life and work of an important Iranian mathematician and highlight his often-overlooked contributions to differential geometry.
method: Historical analysis combined with a modern mathematical exposition of Hachtroudi's results, including the canonical projective connection and its connections to Cartan and parabolic geometry.
result: Presents Hachtroudi's mathematical legacy and its ongoing influence on geometric structures.
conclusion: The paper emphasizes Hachtroudi's role as a pioneer in Iranian mathematics and the lasting significance of his geometric ideas.

title: Explanations, Prompts, And Formalizations: Arguments For New Norms In LLM-Enabled Mathematical Research
authors: Axel Boldt
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As several mathematical conjectures have recently been settled using large language models (LLMs), the mathematical community has formulated norms and recommendations regarding the publishing of such results. These norms do not cover the disclosure of the prompts and precise software setup used to obtain those results, nor do they require that results be formalized in a manner that allows for machine verification. I argue that both of these are essential. In addition, since LLM-obtained results may be hard to understand, human authors have the responsibility to invent intuitive explanations.
tldr: The paper argues for new publishing norms in LLM-assisted mathematical research, including disclosure of prompts, formalization for machine verification, and intuitive explanations.
motivation: Recent LLM-assisted mathematical results have led to norms that omit crucial details like prompts and software setups; the author argues these are essential for reproducibility and understanding.
method: The author presents logical arguments for why disclosure and formalization are necessary, and also emphasizes human responsibility for explanations.
result: The author concludes that prompts and precise software setup should be disclosed, results should be formally verifiable, and human authors should provide intuitive explanations.
conclusion: These norms would improve transparency and trust in LLM-enabled mathematical research.

title: Secrecy Outage Analysis Over Correlated Composite Generalized-Gamma Fading Channels
authors: Muhammad Adil, Pranavkumar Pathak, Salman A. Alqahtani
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates physical-layer security (PLS) over correlated composite generalized-Gamma (GG)/GG fading channels, where both shadowing and small-scale fading follow GG distributions. Using Mellin transforms and Fox-H functions, closed-form expressions are derived for the single-link probability density function (PDF), joint distribution, survival function, and zero-rate secrecy outage probability (SOP)/probability of non-zero secrecy capacity (PNZSC). The general-rate SOP is expressed as an exact double series with one residual onedimensional integral per term. The model includes the Nakagamim/GG and Nakagami-m/Gamma channels as special cases. Numerical results validate the analysis and demonstrate the impact of the fading parameters on secrecy performance.
tldr: The paper derives closed-form expressions for secrecy outage probability over correlated composite generalized-Gamma fading channels using Mellin transforms and Fox-H functions.
motivation: To analyze physical-layer security in wireless fading channels, particularly for composite shadowing and fading scenarios, and to derive tractable expressions for secrecy performance.
method: The authors model the channel with correlated GG/GG distributions, then use Mellin transforms and Fox-H functions to derive statistical distributions and secrecy outage probabilities.
result: They derived closed-form expressions for PDF, joint distribution, survival function, zero-rate SOP and PNZSC, and expressed general-rate SOP as an exact double series. Numerical results validate the analysis and show impact of fading parameters.
conclusion: The derived expressions provide a framework for evaluating secrecy performance in such fading channels, and the model encompasses Nakagami-m/GG and Nakagami-m/Gamma as special cases.

title: Peer Oversight In Collective Decision Making
authors: Pavel Naumov Sarah Mohsen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28754v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article introduces peer [MATH]-oversight, a property of sequential collective decision mechanisms requiring at least [MATH] agents to be responsible for every harmful outcome. It is shown that whenever [MATH]-oversight can be achieved by redistributing control over the decisions in a mechanism, it can be achieved using just [MATH] agents. A polynomial-time algorithm is also presented that determines whether such a redistribution exists and, when it does, constructs one. These results establish peer oversight as a tractable design principle for multiagent decision-making systems.
tldr: This paper introduces peer oversight as a property of collective decision mechanisms and provides an algorithm to achieve it with minimal agents.
motivation: To ensure accountability in multiagent decision-making systems by requiring multiple agents to be responsible for harmful outcomes.
method: Formal modeling of peer oversight and a polynomial-time algorithm for redistributing control to achieve it.
result: Shows that peer oversight can be achieved with just the minimal number of agents and provides an efficient algorithm to find such redistribution.
conclusion: Peer oversight is a tractable design principle for multiagent decision-making systems.

title: Unconditional $V^0_1$-independence Of A Certified Hitting-set Principle
authors: Martin Kol\'a\v{r}
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that a certified formalization of the hitting-set-existence axiom of Atserias and Tzameret, instantiated on the parity-based Nisan-Wigderson compression class of Khaniki, is independent of the two-sorted theory [MATH] of [MATH]-reasoning, unconditionally: [MATH] proves neither it nor its negation. The same holds for the corresponding certified dual weak pigeonhole principle, whose refutation is witnessed by a single seed that certified-computes every string of the model simultaneously. The mechanism is a bounded-arithmetic transfer of Atserias-Tzameret's reduction from hitting sets to the dual weak pigeonhole principle: the amplification half of that reduction, the sole source of its NP-oracle, is unnecessary at the native stretch of the Nisan-Wigderson map, and the compression half becomes a [MATH]-provable implication once circuit evaluation is replaced by its certified [MATH] unfolding. This is, to our knowledge, the first independence result for a derandomization-flavoured existence principle at the [MATH]-reasoning level, and it makes explicit the bridge between the Khaniki Nisan-Wigderson line and the Atserias-Tzameret reverse mathematics of hitting sets.
tldr: This paper proves the unconditional independence of a certified hitting-set principle from a two-sorted theory of bounded arithmetic.
motivation: To establish independence results for derandomization-flavoured existence principles in proof complexity and bounded arithmetic.
method: The authors use a bounded-arithmetic transfer of Atserias-Tzameret's reduction from hitting sets to the dual weak pigeonhole principle, showing the amplification step is unnecessary at the native stretch of the Nisan-Wigderson map.
result: The certified hitting-set principle and its negation are both unprovable in the two-sorted theory, marking the first independence result for such a principle at that reasoning level.
conclusion: This work highlights a bridge between Khaniki's Nisan-Wigderson line and Atserias-Tzameret's reverse mathematics, but it is entirely unrelated to the researcher's interests in quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Web Application Firewalls With Machine Learning For Sql Injection Detection
authors: Lilliane Linnet Musoke, Atta Badii, Ahmed Ashlam
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting SQL Injection (SQLi) attacks ranks among the most critical challenges in web application security. This research conducted a systematic literature review to identify the research gaps in this domain and responsively designed and optimised a DistilBERT-Stacked Ensemble pipeline to improve detection efficiency and robustness while reducing false-positive and false-negative rates. Comprehensive pre-processing and tokenisation were performed, DistilBERT embeddings were extracted, and machine-learning and ensemble classifiers were trained and ranked on accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The three best performers (Logistic Regression, XGBoost and SVM) were combined through a neural meta-learner to form a stacked ensemble. The ensemble was hardened with adversarial examples generated by the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM) and tuned with Optuna. The optimised ensemble achieved 99.81% across all reported metrics, closely comparable to the strongest single model (DistilBERT SVM, 99.82%). On the evaluation platform used in this study (Section 3.8), the ensemble classified the full test set in 0.0136s against 1.896s for DistilBERT-SVM, an approximately 140-fold reduction in measured inference latency, while retaining 99.77% accuracy under a single-step FGSM attack. The contribution is the design and validation of a SQLi detector performing with state-of-the-art accuracy at real-time speed and with demonstrated robustness to a single-step FGSM attack, rather than a marginal gain in accuracy. Sensitivity analysis further confirmed the stability of the model. These findings highlight the value of adversarial training and stacked meta-learning in building robust Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) for SQLi detection. For open validation, the dataset, test sets and models are made available at [URL].
tldr: A study on using DistilBERT and stacked ensemble machine learning for SQL injection detection in web application firewalls.
motivation: To improve the detection efficiency and robustness of web application firewalls against SQL injection attacks.
method: Conducted a systematic literature review, extracted DistilBERT embeddings, trained multiple classifiers, combined the best three via a stacked ensemble with a neural meta-learner, hardened with FGSM adversarial examples, and tuned with Optuna.
result: Achieved 99.81% accuracy across all metrics, with a ~140-fold inference speedup compared to the strongest single model (DistilBERT-SVM), and retained 99.77% accuracy under a single-step FGSM attack.
conclusion: Demonstrated that adversarial training and stacked meta-learning are effective for building robust and real-time SQLi detection systems for WAFs.

title: Identity By Design, Demographics By Accident: Demographic Leakage And Suppression In Behavioral Biometric Embeddings
authors: Iyadh Khan, Patrick Nilackshan, Mohamed Aathif, Mohamed Theesan, Sandareka Wickramanayake, Sanka Rasnayaka
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Behavioral biometric authentication (BBA) systems use deep learning models to transform biometric signals, such as eye movements, voice, keystroke/touchstroke dynamics, and gait, into identity embeddings for user authentication. While designed to encode identity, these embeddings may inadvertently reveal sensitive demographic attributes, including gender, age, and height. Consequently, an adversary with access to the authentication model can infer demographic information from biometric signals, including those of users unseen during training or enrollment. In this paper, we present the first systematic audit of demographic leakage in BBA systems, evaluating 11 models across 9 datasets spanning four biometric modalities. We further benchmark four post-hoc suppression methods-Incremental Variable Elimination (IVE), Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion (HSIC), Adversarial Encoder-Decoder (AED), and Protected Attribute Suppression System (PASS) to assess their ability to mitigate demographic leakage while preserving authentication utility. Our analysis reveals substantial variation in leakage and suppressibility across modalities, model architectures, and learning objectives. While voice embeddings exhibit high leakage that can be effectively suppressed, keystroke/touchstroke embeddings exhibit lower leakage but are considerably more difficult to sanitize. These findings highlight a fundamental privacy risk in behavioral biometric authentication and provide insights into the factors governing demographic information suppressibility.
tldr: This paper systematically audits demographic leakage in behavioral biometric authentication systems and benchmarks post-hoc suppression methods to mitigate privacy risks.
motivation: Behavioral biometric embeddings, while designed for identity authentication, may inadvertently leak sensitive demographic attributes (gender, age, height), posing a privacy risk. The authors aim to quantify this leakage and evaluate methods to suppress it without degrading authentication utility.
method: The study evaluates 11 deep learning models across 9 datasets spanning four biometric modalities (eye movement, voice, keystroke/touchstroke, gait), and benchmarks four post-hoc suppression methods (IVE, HSIC, AED, PASS) for mitigating demographic leakage.
result: Voice embeddings exhibit high leakage that can be effectively suppressed, while keystroke/touchstroke embeddings show lower leakage but are harder to sanitize, revealing modality-dependent trade-offs and substantial variation across architectures.
conclusion: Behavioral biometric authentication poses a fundamental privacy risk due to demographic leakage, and the suppressibility of such information varies significantly across modalities, highlighting the need for targeted privacy-preserving techniques.

title: Membership Is Ownership: A Robust Ownership Verification Framework For Diffusion Models
authors: Feng Jiang, Zuobin Xiong, An Huang, Zhipeng Cai, Yingshu Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale diffusion models have fueled numerous profitable downstream applications for AI-related businesses, including visual editing and content creation. Meanwhile, due to the huge amount of resource consumption (e.g., computation and high-quality data) during training, such diffusion models are deemed valuable intellectual property (IP) for tech companies like OpenAI and Google. Yet, the IP assets are vulnerable to various unauthorized uses by adversaries seeking to steal models for customized, usually commercial applications. Some existing approaches have explored IP protection for AI models; however, they mostly face structural limitations in common --- using a training-time watermarking by injecting artifacts in the model, which can impose a measurable utility cost and can be weakened by post-hoc fine-tuning. To address these challenges, this work investigates IP protection (i.e., model ownership verification) for diffusion models in a realistic commercial scenario with minimal model utility loss. Specifically, the proposed method builds a framework for model ownership verification, termed ``{Membership is Ownership} (MiO)'', based on a population-level hypothesis test on a private member evidence dataset. MiO verifies ownership using two criteria: model attribution through membership inference and model separation from public references. Both are tested at [MATH]. We evaluate MiO on DDIM and Stable Diffusion models without modifying the owner model or its sampling pipeline, and report ROC-AUC and true-positive rates at fixed nominal false-positive targets. Furthermore, MiO stays stable under different post-theft fine-tuning and weight perturbation in adversarial scenarios, reflecting better robustness compared to the watermarking methods.
tldr: Proposes a framework for ownership verification of diffusion models using membership inference and hypothesis testing without modifying the model.
motivation: Existing watermarking-based IP protection methods impose utility costs and are vulnerable to fine-tuning attacks.
method: Builds a 'Membership is Ownership' (MiO) framework using population-level hypothesis tests on a private member evidence dataset, with criteria for model attribution and separation from public references.
result: Evaluated on DDIM and Stable Diffusion, achieving high ROC-AUC and true-positive rates, and remaining stable under fine-tuning and weight perturbation.
conclusion: Provides a robust and non-invasive ownership verification method that preserves model utility while resisting common adversarial modifications.

title: Carvy-fl: Client Anticlustering For Robust Voting In Provably Secure Federated Learning
authors: Masaki Nakada, Honoka Anada, Tatsuya Kaneko, Hiroshi Nakamura, Shinya Takamaeda-Yamazaki, Hideki Takase
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative training without directly sharing raw data, but remains vulnerable to malicious clients. Voting-based FL improves robustness by partitioning clients into groups, training one model per group, and aggregating predictions by plurality voting. However, under class-disjoint non-IID data, distribution-oblivious grouping can yield highly variable certified accuracy (CA). We propose CARVY-FL, which estimates client distribution types from one-epoch model updates and uses anticlustering to increase within-group distributional diversity. Under a fixed grouping, CARVY-FL retains the voting-based CA guarantee while increasing vote margins. Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST show higher CA than FLCert. Under BadNets with model replacement, CARVY-FL improves the AUC of 100-ASR by 11.1% and 14.9%, respectively.
tldr: CARVY-FL introduces client anticlustering in voting-based federated learning to improve certified accuracy under non-IID data and adversarial attacks.
motivation: Voting-based federated learning is vulnerable to malicious clients and suffers from low certified accuracy under class-disjoint non-IID data due to distribution-oblivious grouping.
method: The method estimates client distribution types from one-epoch model updates and uses anticlustering to increase within-group diversity while preserving voting-based certification guarantees.
result: Experiments on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST show higher certified accuracy than FLCert, and improved attack success rate reduction under BadNets with model replacement.
conclusion: CARVY-FL effectively enhances robustness and certified accuracy in federated learning, but is unrelated to the specified quantum information research directions.

title: The Art Of Calling The Winner By Asking Just Enough Questions: Competitive Preference Elicitation With Next-Best Queries
authors: Ziqi Yu Nisarg Shah
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study active elicitation of agent preferences for collectively choosing among [MATH] alternatives using prominent voting rules. We focus on the next-best query model, in which an agent responds to a query by revealing their next favorite alternative, and measure the competitive ratio, which is the worst-case ratio between the number of queries made by the active elicitation algorithm and the minimum number of queries needed to reveal the winning alternative(s) in hindsight. We show that sublinear competitive ratios are achievable for many positional scoring rules, whereas every Condorcet-consistent rule has competitive ratio linear in [MATH]. For Borda count, we develop two complementary techniques: level-wise pruning, whose analysis extends to general concave scoring rules, and multi-scale score thresholding, which gives an [MATH] worst-case guarantee for Borda. We also demonstrate strong empirical performance of level-wise pruning on real data.
tldr: This paper studies active preference elicitation using next-best queries and analyzes the competitive ratio for various voting rules.
motivation: To minimize the number of queries needed to determine the winner in collective decision-making under prominent voting rules.
method: Introduces a next-best query model, analyzes competitive ratios theoretically, and proposes two techniques: level-wise pruning and multi-scale score thresholding.
result: Shows sublinear competitive ratios for many positional scoring rules, linear for Condorcet-consistent rules, and provides guarantees for Borda count.
conclusion: The paper advances algorithmic preference elicitation but is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimally Selecting Representative Agents From A Metric Space
authors: Benjamin Cookson, Eva Deltl, Yeeseok Oh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29097v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the problem of proportionally fair clustering, where the goal is to select [MATH] ``centers'' from a metric space that fairly represent a set of agents who also lie in the metric space. Specifically, we focus on finding a clustering satisfying a fairness property known as the Droop core. In the practical special case in which the set of feasible center locations contains every agent location, the previous best-known result guaranteed a [MATH]-approximation of the Droop core, while the best-known lower bound was [MATH]. In this paper, we show that this lower bound is tight and that a clustering in the [MATH]-Droop core always exists. Further, we show that such a clustering can be achieved by only selecting centers from locations in the metric space where an agent resides. We establish this using Scarf's theorem guaranteeing a nonempty core for balanced non-transferable utility games. This result has several interesting corollaries. Most notably, it resolves the [MATH]-plurality problem of Aronov et al. [2021] for general metric spaces. The main result of this paper was generated by [MATH]-[MATH]-[MATH] through a series of interactions with the authors. The authors of this paper verified the generated proof and rewrote it for clarity.
tldr: This paper resolves a tight bound for proportional fair clustering in metric spaces, proving the existence of a 1/3-Droop core clustering.
motivation: To improve guarantees for fair representation in clustering, specifically addressing the Droop core property.
method: Uses balanced non-transferable utility games and Scarf's theorem to prove existence of the desired clustering.
result: Proves tightness of the lower bound and that a clustering in the 1/3-Droop core always exists, achievable by selecting only agent locations.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental algorithmic result for fair clustering, resolving the plurality problem.

title: Auditing And Mitigating Privacy Leakage In Cloud-Edge Collaborative Decoding
authors: Kejia Zhang, Tianyuan Zou, Zixuan GU, Yang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29111v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Applications such as personalized assistance and proprietary document analysis require large language models (LLMs) to generate outputs from private data. Yet powerful LLMs typically cannot be deployed on the resource-constrained devices where private data resides, and uploading private data to cloud-hosted LLMs exposes sensitive information. Recent work addresses this tension with a cloud-edge collaborative decoding paradigm, where private data are kept on the edge with a small language model (SLM) producing next-token distributions, which are fused with predictions from a cloud LLM operating solely on public data. In this paper, we systematically analyze the privacy risks of such a paradigm with a novel evaluation framework using constructed QA datasets, which show that such collaboration can expose substantial private-context information. To address such privacy leakage, we propose CoVeil, a defense mechanism which dynamically optimizes transmitted signals to suppress leakage during decoding time while preserving the collaborative quality. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that CoVeil consistently improves the privacy-utility trade-off over existing baselines by reducing data leakage by up to 87.2%, with minimal accuracy loss.
tldr: This paper analyzes privacy leakage in cloud-edge collaborative decoding with large language models and proposes CoVeil, a defense mechanism that dynamically optimizes transmitted signals to suppress leakage during decoding.
motivation: Cloud-edge collaborative decoding keeps private data on edge devices but may leak private context when fusing with cloud LLM predictions; the paper aims to audit and mitigate this leakage.
method: They construct QA datasets to evaluate privacy risks, and propose CoVeil, which optimizes transmitted signals during decoding to suppress leakage while preserving collaborative quality.
result: CoVeil reduces data leakage by up to 87.2% with minimal accuracy loss, consistently improving the privacy-utility trade-off over baselines.
conclusion: Collaborative decoding can expose private information, but CoVeil effectively mitigates such leakage, enabling safer use of cloud LLMs with edge-held private data.

title: Mechanizing Typed Regulatory Actions For Security Tokens: Semantics, Falsification, And Bounded Evm Evidence
authors: Jinwook Kim
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Security-token standards expose privileged transfer, freezing, recovery, and compliance mechanisms, but a mechanism does not by itself identify the legal effect being executed or the evidence and reversal obligations attached to it. We formalize in Isabelle/HOL a reference execution semantics for the six regulatory-action meanings proposed in ERC-8319: FREEZE, SEIZE, CONFISCATE, LIQUIDATE, RESTRICT, and RECOVER. The model distinguishes applied, rejected, and operational-failure outcomes and mechanizes reversal, replay, epoch, frame, case-local terminality, and receipt properties; the build has no unproved placeholders or added axioms. It proves an external-truth boundary: two concrete worlds that disagree about title, settlement, and entitlement induce the same kernel observation, so those external facts cannot be established from bound inputs. Constructive witnesses and direct mutations show reachability and falsification for the declared fault set. For one ERC-TRUST Solidity/EVM candidate, we report separately scoped Foundry, Certora, Kontrol/KEVM, mutation, deterministic-build, and runtime-identity evidence. The current publication profile qualifies all seven evidence packages and all 49 Core and 24 mandatory Supporting obligations with no partial credit; six optional obligations remain unclaimed. A mechanized abstraction relation is proved unique and functional under pinned-runtime premises, and package and row corollaries yield conditional, profile-scoped refinement theorems from hash-bound certificates. These results do not constitute a complete Isabelle-to-Solidity-to-EVM refinement theorem, compiler correctness, an audit, production readiness, or deployment verification. The contribution is a machine-checked domain semantics and a falsifiable map of what is proved, what is bounded evidence, what is assumed, and what remains open for a regulated-token execution standard.
tldr: This paper formalizes a reference execution semantics for ERC-8319 regulatory actions in Isabelle/HOL, providing machine-checked proofs and bounded EVM evidence for security-token standards.
motivation: Security-token standards lack a precise semantics for regulatory actions (FREEZE, SEIZE, etc.), leading to ambiguity in legal effects and evidence obligations. The author aims to provide a machine-checked domain semantics and a falsifiable map of what is proved.
method: The author uses Isabelle/HOL to define a reference execution semantics, proves properties like reversal and replay, and conducts falsification via constructive witnesses. They also evaluate a Solidity/EVM candidate using multiple tools (Foundry, Certora, KEVM).
result: The build has no unproved placeholders, proves an external-truth boundary, and reports qualified evidence for all core and mandatory obligations. A mechanized abstraction relation is proven unique and functional.
conclusion: The contribution is a formal semantics and evidence map for regulated-token execution, but it does not constitute a complete refinement theorem or audit, leaving open questions for integration with EVM.

title: GhostSplat: Input-Triggered Backdoors For Multi-View-Consistent 3d Content Manipulation In Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting
authors: Yudong Gao, Zongjian Ding, Linghan Chen, Yajing Chen, Yu Xinglin, Jiale Liu, Shan Huang, Mingjun Cheng
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstructs a 3D scene from sparse images in one forward pass. Its shared pretrained weights also expose a supply-chain attack surface. Existing Neural Radiance Field and 3DGS backdoors modify individual scenes and activate at selected viewpoints; they do not install persistent behavior in shared generator weights. We introduce GhostSplat, an input-triggered backdoor that installs such behavior in feed-forward 3DGS. A low-amplitude pattern added to the input images causes the poisoned generator to render an attacker-chosen payload on unseen victim scenes. Anchoring the payload to a 3D point and reprojecting it into each target view makes the payload multi-view consistent. Exact projection onto the generator's representation-specific consistency set leaves a realized payload unchanged because the output already belongs to that set. The GhostSplat training framework succeeds across three architectures (MVSplat, pixelSplat, DepthSplat) and two datasets (RealEstate10K, ACID). Its strongest evaluated injection and deletion settings reach 96% and 100% ASR, respectively, with zero observed false positives while surviving JPEG, blur, and resampling. Defenses that use only that exact projection are therefore insufficient; effective mitigation requires information or intervention beyond same-set consistency projection.
tldr: GhostSplat introduces an input-triggered backdoor attack on feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting models, enabling persistent multi-view-consistent payload injection across unseen scenes.
motivation: Existing backdoors in NeRF and 3DGS only modify individual scenes and are viewpoint-specific, lacking persistence in shared generator weights. Feed-forward 3DGS models are vulnerable to supply-chain attacks due to their pretrained shared weights.
method: The attack adds a low-amplitude pattern to input images, causing the poisoned generator to render an attacker-chosen payload on unseen scenes. The payload is anchored to a 3D point and reprojected to maintain multi-view consistency, leveraging the generator's consistency set.
result: The method achieves up to 96% ASR for injection and 100% for deletion across three architectures and two datasets, with zero false positives and robustness to JPEG, blur, and resampling. Defenses based solely on exact projection are insufficient.
conclusion: Effective mitigation requires additional information or interventions beyond same-set consistency projection, highlighting the need for more robust defenses against such backdoors.

title: A Broadcast Authenticated Encryption With Keyword Search In The Standard Model: Tightly Secure In Multi-User, Multi-Challenge Settings
authors: Sayantan Mukherjee
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: However, no known work considered the functionality requirement in its most realistic setting. We propose a new security definition of BAEKS in the multi-user (with adaptive corruptions) and multi-challenge (both in terms of ciphertext and trapdoor in an interleaved manner) settings. We also study the question of the unforgeability of BAEKS. In fact, our strong hiding requirement already implies a significant amount of unforgeability. We then propose a new BAEKS construction in the bilinear pairing groups. We prove this scheme achieves adaptive tight full-hiding security under (almost) standard MDDH assumptions. Restricting our BAEKS construction for a single receiver also gives an efficient and tightly secure PAEKS construction. We further run experiments to implement and evaluate our scheme.
tags: broadcast authenticated encryption with keyword search
tldr: This paper introduces new security definitions and a construction for broadcast authenticated encryption with keyword search (BAEKS), achieving tight security in multi-user and multi-challenge settings in the standard model.
motivation: Prior BAEKS schemes did not consider realistic multi-user and multi-challenge settings, which are essential for practical deployment.
method: The paper proposes new security definitions and constructs a BAEKS scheme using bilinear pairing groups, proving tight full-hiding security under MDDH assumptions.
result: The proposed scheme achieves adaptive tight full-hiding security in the standard model, and also yields an efficient single-receiver PAEKS scheme. Experimental evaluation confirms efficiency.
conclusion: The work advances BAEKS by providing a secure and efficient construction in realistic adversarial settings, with tight security reductions.
keywords: broadcast authenticated encryption with keyword search

title: Asymmetric Phase Coding Video Watermarking
authors: Fengchen Liu Guang Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing video watermarking systems are symmetric: the party that can verify a mark holds the extractor weights or generator secret and can therefore also embed one. Benchmarks confirm the consequence, reporting that white-box forgery defeats all evaluated methods. We present a training-free video watermark that removes the shared secret. The signer embeds a complete Ed25519 signature into the phase spectrum of the chroma plane; any party holding the 32-byte public key and public per-video metadata verifies offline, with no model, no registry, and no network. The payload, 1024 bits of signed message with error correction, is an order of magnitude above common learned payloads and is carried by three design elements: a run-length temporal layout whose decoder identifies payload groups by correlation and never reads a frame index, a payload-free search that recovers scale, rotation, and translation from the carrier itself, and a closed-loop signing procedure that selects each video's embedding strength by self-verification through the unchanged public verifier. On 1000 uncurated real-world clips the system ships a verifying signature for 99.3% of the corpus and accepts a wrong public key zero times in 1000 attempts. An attack-aware acceptance gate yields embeddings that survive H.264 re-encoding at 100% and 50% rescaling at 97.4% on gated clips. The signature also verifies through a real display and capture loop, an axis absent from published evaluations.
tldr: This paper presents a training-free asymmetric video watermarking scheme that embeds Ed25519 signatures into the phase spectrum, enabling offline verification with only a public key.
motivation: Existing video watermarking systems are symmetric, allowing any verifier to also embed watermarks, which compromises security. The authors aim to remove the shared secret and enable public verification.
method: The method embeds a complete Ed25519 signature into the phase spectrum of the chroma plane using a run-length temporal layout, a payload-free search for geometric corrections, and a closed-loop signing procedure to select embedding strength.
result: On 1000 real-world clips, 99.3% produced verifying signatures, and wrong public keys were never accepted. The watermark survived H.264 re-encoding at 100% and 50% rescaling at 97.4% on gated clips, and also verified through display-capture.
conclusion: The proposed watermarking scheme achieves asymmetric verification, high payload capacity, and robustness, addressing a critical security flaw in current video watermarking systems.

title: Improving Randomized Metric Distortion To 2.3282
authors: Nisarg Shah
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In metric social choice, each voter ranks a set of [MATH] candidates by her distance to them in an unknown metric space. The cost of a candidate is its average distance to the voters. A randomized voting rule must use only the rankings to choose a lottery over candidates. Its distortion is the worst-case ratio between the expected cost under the lottery it returns and the cost of the best candidate. Charikar, Ramakrishnan, Wang, and Wu [JACM 2024] prove an upper bound of [MATH], establishing a constant separation from deterministic rules, for which the best achievable distortion is [MATH]. Independently, Frank [arXiv:2608.17863] and Ye [arXiv:2608.21202] improve the bound to [MATH], using an equal mixture of maximal lottery and Integrated Veto. The existing arguments do not yield a better bound with any mixture of these rules. We break this barrier with a new ingredient, a random-size stable lottery. Let [MATH] be a random variable over the domain of positive integers. A random-size stable lottery [MATH] guarantees that the probability of a random voter preferring any fixed candidate [MATH] to her favorite of [MATH] i.i.d. draws from [MATH] is at most [MATH], where the probability also averages over [MATH]. When [MATH] deterministically, this reduces to the stable [MATH]-lottery of Charikar, Ramakrishnan, Tan, and Wang [EC 2025]; the case [MATH] is precisely a maximal lottery. Their minimax argument for a fixed [MATH] easily generalizes to a random [MATH]. Our main contribution is to show how stability with respect to a random [MATH] can be used to bound distortion. By mixing a suitably chosen random-size stable lottery with Integrated Veto, we get distortion at most [MATH]. The proof combines infinite-dimensional conic linear-programming duality, heuristic nonlinear optimization, and exact rational verification via the Bernstein basis.
tldr: This paper improves the upper bound on randomized metric distortion in social choice to 2.3282 using random-size stable lotteries.
motivation: The research addresses the problem of designing randomized voting rules that minimize worst-case distortion when only ordinal rankings are available, aiming to bridge the gap between deterministic and randomized rules.
method: The authors introduce a random-size stable lottery, generalize a minimax argument, and combine it with the Integrated Veto rule, using conic linear-programming duality and exact rational verification via the Bernstein basis.
result: They achieve a distortion bound of 2.3282, breaking a previous barrier of the equal-mixture approach and improving on earlier bounds.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of randomized voting rules in metric social choice, but is unrelated to quantum information or any of the specified research directions.

title: Transmissive RIS-Assisted Vehicular Direct-to-Satellite Communications: Opportunities, Limitations, And Comparison With Phased Arrays
authors: Wali Ullah Khan, Abdullah Abdullah, Juan Andres Vazquez-Peralvo, Eva Lagunas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article studies transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted architectures. It compares them with electronically steered phased arrays for the deployment of vehicular direct-to-satellite (D2S) communications in future satellite networks. Rather than treating RIS as a direct replacement for phased arrays, we clarify the operating regimes in which RIS can serve as a low-power wavefront-shaping aperture and those in which phased arrays remain preferable because of their high gain and mature beam-tracking capability. Moreover, phased arrays can support multi-beam operation, which is particularly beneficial for dual connectivity and seamless handover. We distinguish analog, digital, and hybrid phased arrays, discuss the relationship between transmissive RIS and reconfigurable transmitarrays, and highlight practical profile, tracking, and link-budget constraints for mobile terminals. The comparison shows that passive RIS offers attractive power efficiency and aperture scalability, active RIS can partially improve the link budget, and phased arrays remain preferable for high-throughput.
tldr: This paper compares transmissive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) with phased arrays for vehicular direct-to-satellite communications, clarifying operating regimes and trade-offs.
motivation: To determine where RIS can serve as a low-power wavefront-shaping aperture versus where phased arrays are preferable for high-gain, multi-beam, and mature beam-tracking in mobile satellite terminals.
method: Analytical comparison of RIS and phased array architectures, including analog/digital/hybrid phased arrays, link-budget analysis, and discussion of practical profile, tracking, and constraints.
result: Passive RIS offers power efficiency and aperture scalability but lower gain; active RIS partially improves link budget; phased arrays remain preferable for high-throughput due to higher gain and multi-beam support.
conclusion: RIS is suitable for low-power applications, but phased arrays are better for high-throughput vehicular satellite connectivity.

title: It's Hard To PArcK
authors: Kyle Burke, Jeffrey Leman, Craig Tennenhouse
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that Partizan Arc Kayles (PArcK), a generalization of Domineering to graphs, is PSPACE-complete via a reduction from Positive CNF and with recently-discovered techniques for creating PArcK positions with high temperature. The reduction uses only red and blue edges.
tldr: The paper proves that Partizan Arc Kayles (PArcK), a graph-based generalization of Domineering, is PSPACE-complete via a reduction from Positive CNF and high-temperature techniques.
motivation: To determine the computational complexity of the combinatorial game Partizan Arc Kayles.
method: The authors use a polynomial-time reduction from Positive CNF and employ recently-discovered techniques for creating PArcK positions with high temperature, using only red and blue edges.
result: They show that PArcK is PSPACE-complete.
conclusion: The PSPACE-completeness result establishes that PArcK is computationally hard, implying no efficient algorithm exists for optimal play unless P = PSPACE.

title: SpatialTrust: A Benchmark For Environmental Risk Recognition In Secure Authentication
authors: Junbin Lu, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Saesha Wadhwa, Yu Ting Hsu, Jenq-Neng Hwang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual environmental risk recognition plays an important role in secure authentication, where a user's surroundings may reveal sensitive information or introduce potential security risks. However, existing evaluations of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) rarely examine whether models can reliably recognize, localize, and explain such risks in spatially grounded authentication scenarios. We present SpatialTrust, a question-answering benchmark for evaluating environmental risk recognition in secure authentication. SpatialTrust assesses five complementary abilities: sensitive factor detection, direct factor identification, indirect factor identification, direct factor explanation, and indirect factor explanation. We evaluate both proprietary and open-source MLLMs and find that current models show limited performance, especially in understanding and explaining indirect risks, indicating that spatial risk awareness remains a challenging capability for MLLMs. In addition, we introduce SpatialTrustGuard, a structured QA-and-audit pipeline that improves Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct from 36.78% to 41.12% overall. Our findings highlight the need for dedicated benchmarks and structured inference methods to improve the trustworthiness of MLLMs in secure authentication.
tldr: Introduces SpatialTrust, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs' environmental risk recognition in secure authentication, finding limited performance and proposing an improved pipeline.
motivation: To address the lack of benchmarks for evaluating multimodal large language models in recognizing spatially grounded environmental risks during secure authentication.
method: Designs a question-answering benchmark assessing five abilities and evaluates proprietary and open-source MLLMs, then introduces a structured QA-and-audit pipeline (SpatialTrustGuard).
result: Current models show limited performance, especially in explaining indirect risks; SpatialTrustGuard improves Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct from 36.78% to 41.12% overall.
conclusion: Highlights the need for dedicated benchmarks and structured inference methods to improve the trustworthiness of MLLMs in secure authentication.

title: Generalized Hamming Weights Of AJ-Gorenstein One-Point Codes
authors: Eliseo Sarmiento-Rosales, Jos\'e Alberto Guzm\'an-Vega, Juan Carlos Jim\'enez-Cervantes
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study generalized Hamming weights along the one-point code flag of an AJ-Gorenstein curve. We organize these weights in a graded array, the zero diagram, whose entries are generalized coweights: the largest numbers of evaluation points on which subcodes of prescribed dimensions vanish simultaneously. Twisted and Wei duality show that each row of the zero diagram determines both the generalized Hamming weights of a lower block of short codes and the missing weights of a reflected upper block of long codes in the GHW diagram of the complete flag. Our main quantitative result is a uniform coverage theorem. For an AJ-Gorenstein curve of genus [MATH] and evaluation length [MATH], the proportion of generalized-weight positions determined exactly throughout the complete flag satisfies [MATH]. Thus more than half of all generalized-weight positions in the complete flag are determined uniformly. For the smallest Suzuki curve, the general and Castle-specific mechanisms together determine [MATH] of the [MATH] positions, giving an exact coverage of [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies generalized Hamming weights for one-point codes on AJ-Gorenstein curves, introducing a zero diagram and proving a coverage theorem that determines a large proportion of weight positions.
motivation: To understand the structure of generalized Hamming weights for algebraic geometry codes, particularly for AJ-Gorenstein curves, and to develop systematic tools for computing them.
method: Introduces a graded array (zero diagram) of generalized coweights, uses twisted and Wei duality to relate weights across the flag, and proves a uniform coverage theorem for the proportion of determined positions.
result: Shows that more than half of all generalized-weight positions in the complete flag are determined uniformly, with exact coverage for the smallest Suzuki curve.
conclusion: Provides new insights into generalized Hamming weights for a class of algebraic geometry codes and offers a general method for determining them.

title: Linear Coding Of Lti Sources Over Vector Gaussian Channels: A Majorization Approach
authors: Shihao Jin, Junhui Li, Shinji Hara, Wei Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the design of linear time-invariant (LTI) encoder-decoder pairs for transmitting the state of a discrete-time LTI vector source over power-constrained parallel Gaussian channels with feedback. Two types of power constraints are considered. Under individual subchannel power constraints, a necessary and sufficient condition for designing an encoder-decoder pair that achieves bounded estimation error covariance (EEC) is established via two coupled majorization inequalities involving the subchannel signal-to-noise ratios and the antistable poles of the source. Under total channel power constraint, we derive the minimum total power required for a feasible encoder-decoder design by exploiting partial-order progamming under majorization order. An analytical optimal power allocation is obtained for the case of equal noise variances, which admits a water-filling interpretation; for general noise case, a sequential water-filling algorithm is developed. Our results reveal that the difficulty of transmitting a discrete-time LTI source via LTI coding is governed not only by its topological entropy, but also by the evenness of the log-magnitudes of its antistable poles. The design methods for feasible encoder-decoder pairs are also provided.
tldr: Designs linear time-invariant encoder-decoder pairs for transmitting an LTI source over Gaussian channels with feedback, using majorization to characterize feasibility and optimal power allocation.
motivation: To achieve bounded estimation error covariance in LTI source transmission over power-constrained Gaussian channels, extending classical results to vector sources with individual and total power constraints.
method: Uses coupled majorization inequalities to establish necessary and sufficient conditions for feasible design, and partial-order programming under majorization order to derive optimal power allocation, including analytical water-filling for equal noise and an iterative algorithm for general noise.
result: Provides feasibility conditions and optimal power allocation strategies, revealing that feasibility also depends on the evenness of log-magnitudes of antistable poles, not just topological entropy.
conclusion: The paper advances classical control and communication theory but is unrelated to quantum information or related fields, thus not relevant to the stated research interests.

title: Multi-Access Speculative Inference: Uplink Or Downlink?
authors: Kaibin Huang Chang Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-access speculative inference (Multi-SPIN) extends SPIN to multi-device edge networks to accelerate cooperative token generation. It allows on-device small language models (SLMs) to autoregressively draft multiple tokens for individual generation tasks, while an edge-server large language model (LLM) verifies them in parallel. The major communication overhead arises when a drafted token is rejected by the server, in which case sampling the correction token requires access to both the SLM-output draft distribution and the LLM-output target distribution over the full token vocabulary. Existing designs typically perform correction at the server by uploading the draft distribution, but transmitting a vocabulary-wide distribution creates a critical uplink (UL) bottleneck. Alternatively, the correction can be performed at the device by downloading the target distribution, leveraging the high transmission rates available on the downlink (DL). Motivated by this insight, we introduce communication-mode selection as a new design dimension for Multi-SPIN. Specifically, each device can adaptively switch between the UL and DL modes to balance the UL bottleneck against the shared DL resource constraint, thereby relieving the overall communication burden. We formulate a sum-token-goodput maximization problem that jointly accounts for mode selection, draft-length control, and power allocation. For mode selection, we reveal a simple optimal structure that enables efficient search over the number of UL devices, with the corresponding transmit powers optimized accordingly. For draft-length control, we develop a greedy-search algorithm that adapts device-specific draft lengths to heterogeneous computation and communication capabilities. Experimental results on Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek-R1 model pairs demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves token goodput.
tldr: This paper proposes a communication-mode selection framework for multi-access speculative inference to reduce uplink/downlink bottlenecks and improve token generation efficiency.
motivation: Speculative inference in edge networks suffers from communication overhead when correcting drafted tokens, and existing designs create an uplink bottleneck.
method: The paper introduces adaptive uplink/downlink mode selection, draft-length control, and power allocation, formulated as a sum-token-goodput maximization problem with efficient algorithms.
result: Experiments on Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek-R1 model pairs show significant improvements in token goodput.
conclusion: Communication-mode selection is a valuable new design dimension for multi-access speculative inference, effectively reducing communication burdens.

title: The Complexity Of Coverability-Like Problems In Elementary Object Systems: Data-Nets To The Rescue
authors: Francesco Di Cosmo, Soumodev Mal, Tephilla Prince
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Elementary Object Systems (EOSs) are a model in the nets-within-nets (NWNs) paradigm, where tokens in turn can host standard Petri nets. We study the complexity of coverability-like problems, including termination and boundedness, over EOSs. Since coverability and boundedness are undecidable in general on EOSs, we focus on the relevant fragment of conservative EOSs (cEOSs). Our technique interprets cEOSs into the framework of data nets, whose tokens carry data from an infinite domain, thus bridging the nesting and the data-aware paradigms. Specifically, we show that cEOS coverability-like problems are equivalent to the coverability-like problems over an interesting fragment, called channel-[MATH]PNs (c-[MATH]PNs), of data nets that extends [MATH]PN (featuring globally fresh name creation) with restricted forms of transfers with renaming. c-[MATH]PNs remain less expressive than Unordered Data Nets, which feature lossy name creation as well as powerful forms of whole-place operations and broadcasts. These reductions allow us to analyze cEOS coverability taking advantage of known results on data nets. We conclude that the complexity of cEOS coverability is double-Ackermanian, [MATH]-complete, while termination and boundedness are non-primitive recursive.
tldr: This paper analyzes the complexity of coverability-like problems for Elementary Object Systems, showing they are equivalent to certain data nets and establishing double-Ackermannian complexity.
motivation: The authors study Elementary Object Systems, an extension of Petri nets with nested tokens, and note that coverability and boundedness are undecidable in general, so they focus on the conservative fragment to obtain decidability and complexity results.
method: They interpret conservative EOSs into the framework of data nets with globally fresh name creation and restricted transfers, defining a fragment called channel-[MATH]PNs, and use known results on data nets to derive complexity upper bounds.
result: They show that cEOS coverability is double-Ackermannian (and [MATH]-complete), while termination and boundedness are non-primitive recursive.
conclusion: The reductions allow analyzing cEOS coverability using data net techniques, yielding tight complexity bounds.

title: HSMLog: Small Language Model-Assisted Hardware Security Module Log Anomaly Detection With Behavioral Analysis
authors: Chia-Hsuan Wu, Dar-Hsin Dustin Wu, Rui Fang, Yi-Ting Lee, Chia-Chih Lin, Ming-Syan Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware Security Module (HSM) logs capture security-critical behavior, but anomalies emerge from relationships across event sequences, keys, object states, sessions, and temporal patterns rather than isolated events. Existing methods separate detection from HSM-specific evidence validation and reporting. In this paper, we present HSMLog, a two-stage framework for HSM log anomaly detection with retrieval-grounded behavioral analysis. In Stage 1, a small language model (SLM) identifies candidate alerts from sliding windows of structured HSM events and performs policy-guided assessment using HSM-specific operational rules. In Stage 2, retrieved policies and historical suspicious-key records strictly predating the alert window, together with candidate-related log context, support conservative candidate review and incident analysis. Evaluated on real industrial HSM background logs augmented with anomaly scenarios co-defined with industrial partners, HSMLog achieves 98.97% precision, 96.00% recall, 98.66% anomalous-event coverage, and a 97.46% F1 score, demonstrating effective anomaly alerting and incident triage in the studied setting.
tldr: HSMLog is a two-stage framework using a small language model for hardware security module log anomaly detection, incorporating policy-guided assessment and behavioral analysis.
motivation: Anomalies in HSM logs arise from complex relationships across events, keys, sessions, and temporal patterns, and existing methods fail to integrate HSM-specific evidence validation and reporting.
method: Stage 1 uses a small language model to identify candidate alerts from sliding windows of structured HSM events and performs policy-guided assessment. Stage 2 retrieves policies and historical suspicious-key records to support conservative candidate review and incident analysis.
result: Achieves 98.97% precision, 96.00% recall, 98.66% anomalous-event coverage, and a 97.46% F1 score on real industrial HSM logs with augmented anomaly scenarios.
conclusion: The framework demonstrates effective anomaly alerting and incident triage in the studied setting, showing potential for practical HSM security monitoring.

title: Polyflow: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework For Static Cross-Language Information Flow Analysis
authors: Haoran Yang, Zhixuan Zhong, Jiawei Guo, Haipeng Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern software systems are commonly constructed in multiple, interacting programming languages. This construction leads to additional, often stealthy vulnerabilities buried in complex information flow due to language interactions. Existing static analyzers are impeded by the heterogeneous semantics of different languages, whereas dynamic approaches suffer from the limited coverage of (available and/or generated) test inputs. In this paper, we develop PolyFlow, a neural-symbolic framework for statically reasoning about information flow across language boundaries, combining large language models (LLMs) and static analysis synergistically. Governed by the control-flow representation of a given multi-language system, PolyFlow leverages LLMs to identify implicit flow facts due to challenging language features, hence augmenting the base representation and then propagating data flow through the system. It tackles inherent barriers (e.g., token limit and hallucination) of LLMs by putting them under careful guidance (e.g., static-analysis-guided scoping, context management, and fact checking), along with a multi-LLM expert panel for negotiated validation. Our experiments on real-world Python-C and Java-C systems show that PolyFlow is cost-effective and superior to various kinds of state-of-the-art baselines, revealing previously unknown cross-language vulnerabilities that are missed by all the baselines.
tldr: PolyFlow is a neuro-symbolic framework that combines LLMs and static analysis to detect cross-language information flow vulnerabilities.
motivation: Modern software systems are multilingual, leading to stealthy vulnerabilities that existing static and dynamic analyzers miss.
method: PolyFlow uses LLMs to identify implicit flow facts and augment control-flow representation, guided by static analysis and validated by a multi-LLM expert panel.
result: Experiments on Python-C and Java-C systems show PolyFlow outperforms baselines and uncovers previously unknown vulnerabilities.
conclusion: The neural-symbolic approach effectively addresses cross-language information flow analysis, demonstrating cost-effectiveness and superiority over existing methods.

title: Random Attractors And Almost-sure Stability Under Discretization Of A Stochastic Autoparametric System
authors: Chuchu Chen, Jialin Hong, Yibo Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a stochastic autoparametric block-and-pendulum system, the long-time dynamics exhibit two fundamental features: the almost-sure stability of the single mode solution, characterized by its Lyapunov exponent, and the global asymptotic dynamics when this single mode solution loses stability. This naturally raises the question of whether these dynamical features are preserved under discretization, since such preservation is essential for the resulting discrete system to faithfully capture the qualitative behavior of the continuous system. To address this question, we first establish the existence of a random attractor for the continuous system subject to multiplicative stochastic excitation, providing a rigorous characterization of the global asymptotic dynamics. We then propose a numerical discretization that induces a discrete random dynamical system and prove the convergence of its random attractor to the continuous one as the step size tends to zero. In addition, we show that the numerical Lyapunov exponent of the single mode solution has the same sign as its continuous counterpart for sufficiently small step sizes, thus preserving the corresponding almost-sure stability or instability classification. These results demonstrate that the proposed discretization captures both the global asymptotic dynamics and the stability characteristics of the underlying stochastic autoparametric system.
tldr: This paper analyzes the long-time dynamics of a stochastic autoparametric system under discretization, proving convergence of random attractors and preservation of almost-sure stability.
motivation: To ensure that numerical discretizations faithfully capture the qualitative behavior of stochastic dynamical systems, specifically the global asymptotic dynamics and stability characteristics.
method: Establishes existence of a random attractor for the continuous system with multiplicative noise, proposes a numerical discretization, proves convergence of discrete random attractors to the continuous one, and analyzes the sign of the numerical Lyapunov exponent.
result: The proposed discretization preserves both the global asymptotic dynamics (via random attractor convergence) and the almost-sure stability/instability classification for sufficiently small step sizes.
conclusion: The discretization captures the essential dynamical features of the stochastic autoparametric system, validating its use for numerical studies.

title: Hardness Of Approximation Of Rank Aggregation On Ulam Metric
authors: Sk Ruhul Azgor, Diptarka Chakraborty, Le van Cuong, Debarati Das, Tien Long Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximability of rank aggregation under the Ulam metric. In the problem, the goal is to find a permutation minimizing the sum of its Ulam distances to the input permutations, while in the problem the objective is to minimize the maximum such distance. Both problems are known to be NP-hard, but no explicit approximation hardness was previously known. We prove that, for every [MATH], it is NP-hard to approximate either Ulam median or Ulam center within a factor of [MATH], even when the input consists of only four permutations. We further show that unless P = NP, neither problem admits a polynomial-time additive approximation scheme. The hardness result for Ulam median is established via a reduction from MAX-E3-LIN-2. The corresponding hardness for Ulam center is then obtained through a reduction from Ulam median.
tldr: This paper proves that approximation of rank aggregation under the Ulam metric (Ulam median and Ulam center) is NP-hard within any constant factor, even for four input permutations.
motivation: The problems are NP-hard but explicit approximation hardness was unknown; the authors aim to establish strong inapproximability results.
method: They reduce MAX-E3-LIN-2 to Ulam median and then Ulam median to Ulam center.
result: For every constant factor, it is NP-hard to approximate either problem, and no polynomial-time additive approximation scheme exists unless P=NP.
conclusion: The results settle the approximation complexity of these problems by showing they are hard to approximate beyond any constant factor.

title: Emergent Behavior And Uncertainty In IoT-Enhanced Business Processes: Challenges And Future Directions
authors: Marco Pegoraro, Sara Pettinari, Ivan Compagnucci, Marco Franceschetti, Ronny Seiger
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: IoT-enhanced business processes are characterized by high complexity due to heterogeneous actors, varying levels of autonomy among participating systems, continuously evolving execution contexts spanning the digital and physical worlds, and continuous event streams. In such settings, process behavior partially emerges only at runtime through complex interactions involving humans, IoT devices, physical objects, software systems, agents, and services. This complexity introduces partial observability, uncertainty, and runtime dynamics that are difficult to anticipate and that challenge traditional business process management (BPM) assumptions and systems. We discuss these challenges from three perspectives, addressing 1) uncertainty representation, 2) operationalization of IoT-enhanced processes, and 3) runtime management of emergent behavior. Based on a motivating scenario and an analysis of the state of the art, we identify open research gaps and outline short-, medium-, and long-term recommendations to shape a research agenda on emergent behavior in IoT-enhanced business processes.
tldr: This paper discusses challenges and research directions for handling emergent behavior and uncertainty in IoT-enhanced business processes.
