motivation: To address the complexity and unpredictability introduced by IoT devices and dynamic environments in business process management.
method: They analyze the state of the art, present a motivating scenario, and outline open research gaps with short-, medium-, and long-term recommendations.
result: They identify open research gaps and propose a research agenda to manage emergent behavior and uncertainty.
conclusion: There is a need for novel approaches and systems to effectively handle emergent behavior and uncertainty in IoT-enhanced business processes.

title: Benchmark Contamination: A Taxonomy Organized By Defeated Mitigation
authors: Johanna Angulo, V\'ictor Yeste, Hector Espinos-Morato
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A benchmark score is a joint property of the model, the evaluation harness, the elicitation budget, the sampled population, and contamination status. Leaderboards publish the model and the score, so capability and leakage stay observationally equivalent. Existing taxonomies classify contamination for automated detection, not the question a reporter faces at publication: given the mitigations already applied, which validity threats remain open? We introduce a taxonomy organized by the mitigation each type defeats -- direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, and acquired -- spanning training-time and evaluation-time leakage. Holding out a private test set closes the first alone. The fifth is acquired during the evaluation itself; because it is a property of one run, it must be recorded with the reported score rather than with the benchmark release. We operationalize it as a four-field disclosure protocol in which "unknown" is a valid entry, released under CC BY 4.0 with a JSON Schema, a validator, and worked examples. Two coders external to the design team applied a pre-registered instrument to 41 documents. Per-variable linear-weighted [MATH] runs from 0.00 to 0.35 (median 0.21) over 29 main-pass documents against a single-coder test-retest ceiling of 0.84, collapsing under the class skew the registration anticipated; pooling raises it to 0.46 through chance correction rather than better agreement. Two variables fall below the prevalence-robust threshold registered in advance: strata reporting and the acquired type introduced here. Disagreement concentrates on when a variable applies rather than on what a document states. Elicitation budgets are reported in 13% of documents, and no document addresses all five types. The contribution is the taxonomy, the score-side artifact that follows from it, and a pre-registered measurement of instrument reliability and current disclosure.
tldr: This paper proposes a taxonomy for benchmark contamination organized by the mitigation each type defeats, along with a disclosure protocol, and measures inter-coder reliability.
motivation: Existing taxonomies of benchmark contamination focus on automated detection, but the authors address the question of which validity threats remain open given mitigations already applied at publication time.
method: They introduce a five-type taxonomy (direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, acquired), operationalize the acquired type as a four-field disclosure protocol, and apply a pre-registered instrument with two external coders to 41 documents.
result: Inter-coder agreement was low (median linear-weighted kappa 0.21), collapsing under class skew, with two variables falling below the prevalence-robust threshold; elicitation budgets are rarely reported.
conclusion: The main contributions are the taxonomy, the score-side artifact (disclosure protocol), and a pre-registered measurement of instrument reliability, which highlights current poor reporting practices.

title: Oasis: Optimizing Attacker Sequences For Hard-Label Black-Box Text Attacks
authors: Qian Chen, Shiliang Xiao, Yuzhi Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Different attack methods follow different search trajectories, they succeed on different subsets of samples, whereas existing hard-label black-box text attacks mainly focus on improving individual attackers or manually combining them. We present {\OURS}, a method for optimizing attacker sequences in hard-label black-box text attacks. {\OURS} first performs a one-time bi-objective attack chain search over candidate sequences to balance attack success rate and perturbation, and then reuses the selected fixed global chain during attack chain execution. Experiments across multiple datasets, victim models, and large language models show that {\OURS} consistently outperforms strong standalone baselines and simple manually constructed chains. These results suggest that attacker composition is not merely an implementation choice, but a practical optimization target for improving hard-label black-box text attacks.
tldr: This paper presents Oasis, a method for optimizing attack sequences in hard-label black-box text attacks, balancing success rate and perturbation.
motivation: Existing hard-label black-box text attacks focus on individual attackers or manual combinations, but never optimize the order of attacks. The authors argue that attacker composition is an under-explored optimization target.
method: Oasis performs a one-time bi-objective attack chain search over candidate sequences to balance attack success rate and perturbation, then reuses the selected fixed global chain during execution.
result: Experiments across datasets, victim models, and large language models show that Oasis consistently outperforms standalone baselines and manual chains.
conclusion: The results suggest that automating attacker sequence selection is a practical way to improve hard-label black-box text attacks.

title: A Proof Of The Matrix Spencer Conjecture
authors: Suvrit Sra Emrullah Akbas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a novel approach to matrix discrepancy based on matrix small-ball estimates. Specifically, we use a determinantal weight (obtained from the log-barrier) to scale the small-ball probability into a partition function of a tilt of the Gaussian measure. We then employ matrix-weighted Poincar\'e inequalities to compare this partition function to that of a pinched or diagonal part of the matrix, obtaining constants. Our technique yields a hereditary small-ball estimate for Gaussian series that should be of independent interest. As the main application, we resolve the Matrix Spencer conjecture: for symmetric [MATH] matrices [MATH] with [MATH], one can efficiently find a coloring [MATH] with [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves the Matrix Spencer conjecture using new matrix small-ball estimates based on determinantal weights and matrix-weighted Poincaré inequalities.
motivation: To resolve a long-standing conjecture about discrepancy for symmetric matrices, which has applications in combinatorial optimization and algorithmic theory.
method: They develop a novel approach using matrix small-ball estimates, determinantal weights (from log-barrier), and matrix-weighted Poincaré inequalities to compare partition functions, leading to a hereditary small-ball estimate.
result: They prove the Matrix Spencer conjecture: for symmetric matrices with entries bounded in [-1,1], one can efficiently find a coloring with discrepancy bounded by O(√n) (the exact bound is not specified in the abstract).
conclusion: The technique yields a hereditary small-ball estimate of independent interest and resolves the conjecture.

title: Full Topological Entropy Of Xiong Chaotic Sets Beyond The Specification Property
authors: Xinyun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that for a shift dynamical system [MATH] with a weakened form of the specification property, there exists a Xiong chaotic set [MATH] of [MATH] with full topological entropy everywhere (i.e. the intersection of [MATH] and arbitrary non-empty open subset of [MATH] has full topological entropy). Moreover, [MATH] satisfies that for any non-empty subset [MATH] and any continuous map [MATH] there exists an increasing sequence [MATH] of positive integers such that [MATH] holds for any [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves the existence of Xiong chaotic sets with full topological entropy in shift dynamical systems under a weakened specification property.
motivation: To understand how specification properties affect the distribution of chaos in topological dynamics.
method: The author constructs a Xiong chaotic set using symbolic dynamics techniques for shifts with a weakened specification property.
result: It is shown that there exists a Xiong chaotic set whose intersection with any non-empty open subset has full topological entropy, and it also satisfies a condition involving continuous maps.
conclusion: The result generalizes known theorems and demonstrates that full entropy chaos can occur beyond the standard specification property.

title: A Note On A Sparse Sampling Conjecture
authors: Sinai Robins Oleg Asipchuk
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A conjecture made by the second author was that two convex, centrally symmetric bodies of positive measure which are not multi-tilers must agree up to a rigid motion whenever the Fourier transforms of their indicator functions agree on \(\Z^d\). Counterexamples were constructed by the first author in dimensions \(d\geq4\), showing that the lattice \(\Z^d\) can be too sparse. Here we show that the initial conjecture is also false in the remaining dimensions \(2\) and \(3\). However, we prove a related positive result, with a stronger conclusion and without either central symmetry or the non-multitiling assumption. Let \(\mathcal L\subset\R^d\) be a full-rank lattice, and let \(\mathcal P,Q\subset\R^d\) be connected finite unions of convex bodies such that no two distinct points of either set are congruent modulo \(\mathcal L\). If the Fourier transforms of their indicator functions agree on the dual lattice \(\mathcal L^*\), then \(Q=\mathcal P+\ell\) for some \(\ell\in \mathcal L\). In particular, if both sets are symmetric about the origin, then \(\mathcal P=Q\).
tldr: The paper disproves a conjecture about convex bodies' Fourier transforms agreeing on a lattice in dimensions 2 and 3, and proves a related positive result for full-rank lattices.
motivation: To settle a conjecture on when two convex centrally symmetric bodies are congruent if their Fourier transforms agree on the integer lattice.
method: Construct counterexamples in dimensions 2 and 3, and prove a positive result for connected finite unions of convex bodies under a lattice congruence condition.
result: The initial conjecture is false in all dimensions, but a stronger conclusion holds without central symmetry or non-multitiling assumptions.
conclusion: The initial conjecture fails, but a modified version holds for general lattices, providing a new theorem in harmonic analysis and geometry of numbers.

title: A Comprehensive Survey On Linguistic Steganography: Methods, Countermeasures, Evaluation, And Challenges
authors: Ruiyi Yan, Chenhui Chu, Zhongliang Yang, Yugo Murawaki
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linguistic steganography hides secret messages in natural language text. Large language models (LLMs) have reshaped the field, but a systematic account of how these scattered advances collectively reshape the field in this new era is still missing. We provide one along four axes: 148 steganographic methods, 60 linguistic steganalysis countermeasures, 23 evaluation metrics, and 9 open challenges, each with taxonomies, reviews, and adoption analyses. Cutting across these axes, we identify five specific paradigm shifts in the LLM era: (1) from covertext modification to prompt-only generation, (2) from heuristic to provable security, (3) from white-box symmetric LMs to black-box or asymmetric access, (4) from security-centric designs to joint optimization, and (5) from text-quality concerns to engineering issues. The survey aims to serve as both a reference and a roadmap for practical and responsible linguistic steganography in the LLM era.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of linguistic steganography in the LLM era, covering methods, countermeasures, evaluation metrics, and open challenges.
motivation: The field has been reshaped by LLMs, but a systematic account of these changes is missing.
method: The survey analyzes 148 steganographic methods, 60 steganalysis countermeasures, 23 evaluation metrics, and 9 challenges, and identifies five paradigm shifts.
result: It provides taxonomies, reviews, and adoption analyses, and outlines the paradigm shifts.
conclusion: The paper serves as a reference and roadmap for practical and responsible linguistic steganography in the LLM era.

title: Reactive Peripheral Modeling For Faithful Firmware Rehosting
authors: Qinying Wang, Florian Hofhammer, Eduard Vlad, Jianqiang Wang, Marcel Busch, Shouling Ji, Mathias Payer
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rehosting enables tight control and introspection for firmware testing, but existing approaches largely fail to reach deeper application states and cannot drive embedded protocol stacks beyond early-stage initialization. This limitation reflects a broader weakness in current rehosting techniques: their inability to faithfully model complex peripheral semantics and dependencies. In particular, existing work typically relies on passive approximations of peripheral behavior and overlooks three key aspects: (i) the interplay among interrupts, MMIO, and DMA; (ii) implicit state transitions within peripherals; and (iii) interactions across multiple peripherals. To address this challenge, we propose Reactive Peripheral Modeling (RPM), an abstraction that models hardware peripherals as reactive and stateful systems. RPM captures peripheral behavior using event-condition-action semantics, enabling faithful representation of interrupt, MMIO, and DMA scheduling, implicit state transitions, and cross-peripheral interactions. We implement RPM in Bluezz for BLE firmware rehosting and fuzzing, and show that reactive modeling is necessary to reach deep protocol states. We evaluate Bluezz on representative BLE stacks, including NimBLE, Zephyr, and Nordic SoftDevice, a closed-source commercial stack. Across 18 targets, Bluezz achieves an average basic-block coverage more than 2.6 times that of prior state-of-the-art rehosting approaches. Unlike prior approaches, which remain largely confined to advertising and scanning logic, Bluezz reliably exercises connected BLE states and uncovers five previously unknown vulnerabilities that manifest only after connection establishment. Finally, we show that RPM generalizes beyond BLE to other embedded firmware running on different MCUs.
tldr: This paper proposes Reactive Peripheral Modeling (RPM) for faithful firmware rehosting, enabling deep state exploration in embedded protocols like BLE.
motivation: Existing firmware rehosting techniques fail to reach deep application states due to inaccurate peripheral modeling, ignoring interrupts, MMIO, DMA, and state transitions.
method: RPM models peripherals as reactive stateful systems using event-condition-action semantics, implemented in Bluezz for BLE rehosting and fuzzing.
result: Bluezz achieves 2.6x better basic-block coverage than prior methods across 18 targets and finds five new vulnerabilities after connection establishment.
conclusion: Reactive peripheral modeling is necessary for faithful rehosting and generalizes beyond BLE to other embedded firmware.

title: Shadowing And Inverse Shadowing In Spaces Retractable Onto Graphs
authors: Elyssa Stephens Jonathan Meddaugh
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we show that shadowing and inverse shadowing are generic properties for spaces in which there exists an [MATH]-retraction onto a graph for any [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that shadowing and inverse shadowing are generic properties for spaces that retract onto a graph.
motivation: To understand when shadowing properties are typical in dynamical systems.
method: The authors use retraction onto graphs to establish genericity.
result: Shadowing and inverse shadowing are shown to be generic for such spaces.
conclusion: These properties are common in spaces that retract onto graphs.

title: High-Order-Accurate Continuity Enforcing Nystr\"om Discretization Of 3d Maxwell Combined Field Integral Equations
authors: Bernd Hofmann, Reza Molavi, Constantine Sideris
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Nystr\"om-collocation discretizations of the electric field integral equation (EFIE), the surface divergence acts on surface densities that may be discontinuous across patch boundaries, which degrades accuracy and convergence. We show that this not only affects the EFIE but every formulation in which the operator occurs, either in the equation itself or in the scattered field computation, and propose a high-order-accurate continuity-enforcing scheme for smooth surfaces as a remedy for the direct and indirect EFIEs, magnetic field integral equations (MFIEs), and regularized combined field integral equations (CFIEs) alike. The scheme comprises two ingredients: i) We show how to discretize the equations via a Chebyshev-based Nystr\"om scheme, which admits closed quadrature rules. ii) Since unknowns and test vectors are in terms of patch-local curvilinear bases, continuity is enforced by a change of basis: we construct sparse mapping matrices assembled solely from the curvilinear geometry description. In doing so, we restore the accuracy of the EFIE such that it can be combined with the MFIEs with equal weights to form CFIEs. Numerical studies for the scattering from canonical and realistic geometries show that all considered formulations individually and combined benefit from the continuity enforcement in terms of better conditioning, reduced iterations of an iterative solver, and several more digits of accuracy in the scattered fields, despite reducing the total number of unknowns.
tldr: This paper presents a high-order-accurate Nyström discretization method for solving 3D Maxwell combined field integral equations by enforcing continuity across patch boundaries.
motivation: The surface divergence in Nyström-collocation discretizations of integral equations can act on discontinuous surface densities, degrading accuracy and convergence for EFIE, MFIE, and CFIE formulations.
method: The authors propose a Chebyshev-based Nyström scheme with closed quadrature rules and a sparse change-of-basis mapping to enforce continuity of unknowns and test vectors across patch boundaries using only the curvilinear geometry.
result: Numerical tests on canonical and realistic geometries show that continuity enforcement improves conditioning, reduces iterations, and yields several more digits of accuracy in scattered fields while decreasing the total number of unknowns.
conclusion: The proposed continuity-enforcing scheme restores high-order accuracy for all considered integral equation formulations and is beneficial for both individual and combined equations.

title: A General Superconvergence Result For Cubature On Triangulated Polygonal Domains
authors: Jonah A. Reeger
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cubature rules, which approximate definite integrals as a linear combination of a set of function values, are ubiquitous and necessary for computational methods in the physical sciences. A superconvergence result for cubature rules on polygonal domains is developed, whereby a rule that is exact for all bivariate polynomials of a fixed even degree realize an extra order of convergence under a decrease in the spacing between nodes.
tldr: This paper presents a superconvergence result for cubature rules on triangulated polygonal domains, demonstrating extra convergence order with decreasing node spacing.
motivation: Cubature rules are essential for computational methods in physical sciences, and understanding their convergence can improve efficiency.
method: The author develops a general superconvergence result for cubature rules on polygonal domains, assuming exactness for bivariate polynomials of fixed even degree.
result: It shows that such rules achieve an extra order of convergence when node spacing decreases.
conclusion: This provides a theoretical foundation for designing more efficient cubature rules in numerical integration.

title: Transfinite Schreier Families And Cardinal Invariants
authors: Christian Rosendal Kevin Beanland
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the dependence of the transfinite Schreier hierarchy on the choice of fundamental sequences for the countable limit ordinals. With each Schreier family we associate an interval endpoint function. We prove that the bounding number is equal to [MATH] exactly when the fundamental sequences may be chosen so that these endpoint functions form an unbounded family in the eventual domination order. Equivalently, the hierarchy then satisfies the tail-covering property isolated by Shiliaev, or every infinite compact interval family has infinite intersection with some member of the hierarchy. We also prove that the dominating number is equal to [MATH] exactly when the fundamental sequences may be chosen so that every compact family of finite subsets of [MATH] is contained in one Schreier family. The latter equivalence combines Fremlin's cofinality theorem for compact subsets of the rationals with an absorption construction for compact families.
tldr: This paper studies the dependence of the transfinite Schreier hierarchy on fundamental sequences for countable limit ordinals, linking it to cardinal invariants such as bounding and dominating numbers.
motivation: To understand how the properties of the Schreier hierarchy depend on the choice of fundamental sequences, and to connect this to cardinal invariants in set theory.
method: The authors introduce interval endpoint functions, and use the tail-covering property, Shiliaev's isolation, and an absorption construction, along with Fremlin's cofinality theorem for compact subsets of rationals.
result: They prove that the bounding number equals a certain cardinal exactly when fundamental sequences can be chosen so that endpoint functions form an unbounded family in eventual domination order, and similarly for the dominating number.
conclusion: The paper establishes equivalences between cardinal invariants and properties of fundamental sequences, showing that the hierarchy satisfies tail-covering or absorption properties under precisely characterized conditions.

title: Gappy Probabilistic Manifold Decomposition For Nonlinear Field Reconstruction
authors: Qihan Feng, Jiaming Guo, Jiarun Meng, Dunhui Xiao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes gappy probabilistic manifold decomposition (Gappy PMD), a nonlinear method for reconstructing high-dimensional fields from extremely sparse measurements. Gappy PMD reconstructs the field on the nonlinear manifold learned by probabilistic manifold decomposition (PMD). We further propose a differentiable point selection method for reduced-order model (ROM)-based field reconstruction (DPS). Using differentiable meshless interpolation within the ROM-based reconstruction framework, DPS makes the full-field reconstruction error differentiable with respect to the sampling locations and directly optimizes these locations. In addition, a theoretical error analysis for Gappy PMD is also given. It splits the squared reconstruction error into two orthogonal parts: one normal to the reconstruction manifold and the other induced by sparse sampling and observation noise. Under a stability condition on the sampling operator, this error vanishes with the PMD approximation error and the noise. The Gappy PMD is evaluated on three numerical test cases: flow past a cylinder, lid-driven cavity flow, and backward-facing step flow. For the same reduced dimension and sampling points, Gappy PMD attains mean relative [MATH] errors one to two orders of magnitude below Gappy POD. Optimizing the sampling points with DPS further improves reconstruction accuracy and robustness.
tldr: Presents a nonlinear method using probabilistic manifold decomposition and optimized sampling for reconstructing high-dimensional fields from sparse measurements.
motivation: To improve field reconstruction accuracy from limited measurement data, addressing limitations of linear methods like Gappy POD.
method: Gappy PMD reconstructs fields on a nonlinear manifold learned by PMD; DPS optimizes sampling locations via differentiable interpolation.
result: Numerical tests show Gappy PMD achieves errors one to two orders of magnitude lower than Gappy POD, with further improvements using DPS.
conclusion: The method effectively enhances nonlinear field reconstruction from sparse data, with theoretical guarantees on error decomposition.

title: Decay Of Correlations And Normal Approximation For Nonstationary Heterochaos Baker Maps
authors: Hiroki Takahasi Juho Lepp\"anen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study statistical properties of nonstationary compositions of a sequence of heterochaos baker maps. For maps whose central direction is mostly expanding, we establish three main results: exponential rate of memory loss for a broad class of measures (Theorem 1.1), a functional correlation bound with stretched exponential decay (Theorem 1.2), and an error bound for the multivariate central limit theorem (CLT) in the Wasserstein-1 distance (Theorem 1.3). The proofs are based on the construction of suitable Gibbs--Markov induced maps for the nonstationary compositions. In a certain special case we obtain a concrete estimate on the rate of convergence in the multivariate CLT (Theorem 1.4).
tldr: This paper analyzes statistical properties of nonstationary compositions of heterochaos baker maps, providing exponential memory loss and stretched exponential correlation decay via Gibbs-Markov induced maps, along with CLT error bounds.
motivation: To understand statistical properties of non-autonomous dynamical systems, specifically for sequences of maps that change over time.
method: The authors construct Gibbs-Markov induced maps for the nonstationary compositions and use them to establish correlation bounds and error bounds for the multivariate central limit theorem.
result: They prove exponential rate of memory loss for a broad class of measures, a functional correlation bound with stretched exponential decay, and an error bound for the multivariate CLT in Wasserstein-1 distance.
conclusion: The paper contributes to ergodic theory of nonstationary systems, providing rigorous rates of convergence and mixing properties.

title: Enhancing Web Application Firewalls With Bert-gnn For Sql Injection Detection
authors: Lilliane Linnet Musoke, Atta Badii, Ahmed Ashlam
abstract: ArXiv:2608.28882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting sophisticated SQL Injection (SQLi) attacks remains among the most critical challenges in web applications security. This research study has resulted in an optimised hybrid BERT-GNN pipeline with improved detection accuracy and robustness while reducing false-positive and false-negative rates. SQL queries are tokenised and encoded into contextual BERT embeddings, which then initialise the node features of a Graph Neural Network (GNN) trained to classify each query, with the architecture tuned by Optuna over accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The proposed model achieved 99.67% accuracy, with 99.71% precision, 99.39% recall, and 99.55% F1-score on the attack class. A sensitivity analysis, performed by perturbing graph inputs, further assessed the model robustness and yielded a low mean sensitivity score of 0.0037, indicating stable predictions under such perturbations. The results have demonstrated the potential of a novel hybrid model that couples BERT contextual understanding with the GNN structural modelling to detect sophisticated SQLi attack vectors. For open validation, the dataset, test sets and models are made available at [URL].
tldr: This paper presents a BERT-GNN hybrid model for detecting SQL injection attacks in web application firewalls, achieving high accuracy and robustness.
motivation: Sophisticated SQL injection attacks remain a critical challenge for web application security, requiring more effective detection methods.
method: The authors tokenize SQL queries, generate contextual BERT embeddings, and use them as node features for a Graph Neural Network (GNN) classifier; architecture hyperparameters are tuned via Optuna.
result: The model achieves 99.67% accuracy with 99.71% precision, 99.39% recall, and 99.55% F1-score on the attack class, and a low sensitivity score of 0.0037 indicates robustness to input perturbations.
conclusion: The hybrid BERT-GNN approach effectively enhances SQLi detection and demonstrates potential for practical deployment in web application firewalls.

title: WoE Wrote It? Watermarking Mixture-of-Experts LLMs For Black-Box Text Provenance
authors: Jona Te Lintelo, Lichao Wu, Stjepan Picek
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) watermarks provide a mechanism for text provenance, enabling model owners to identify machine-generated content and attribute it to a specific watermarked model. However, current LLM watermarking approaches predominantly rely on inference-time sampler methods and focus their analysis on dense models. Inference-time methods are only effective when the text is explicitly generated via the model owner's controlled API; they fail in a post-compromise scenario. An adversary who steals or leaks the model weights gains complete control over inference and can simply run an unmodified sampler, bypassing the watermark and preventing post-theft attribution. In this work, we introduce Watermarking of Experts (WoE), a novel black-box text provenance method that leverages the unique structural properties of sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. WoE biases the vocabulary of specific experts and shifts the watermark signal embedding away from unenforceable inference wrappers. This approach ensures the watermark remains intrinsic to the model parameters, enabling defenders to attribute text generated by stolen weights, leaked checkpoints, and secondary dense models distilled from the stolen architecture without needing access to the adversary's deployment or weights. We evaluate WoE across eight MoE models, demonstrating successful watermark detection from suspect text, achieving an average true positive rate of 90.1% at a 1% false positive rate, reaching up to 94.9%, while largely preserving general model utility. Furthermore, WoE remains detectable under adversarial supervised fine-tuning, model extraction, and output-level paraphrasing, forcing malicious actors into a trade-off in which weakening the attribution signal requires additional model adaptation or text-rewriting operations, or compromises the utility of the resulting output.
tldr: Proposes WoE, a watermarking method for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that embeds a signal in expert biases for black-box text provenance, enabling attribution even after model theft.
motivation: Existing LLM watermarks rely on inference-time wrappers that fail if an adversary gains control of the model weights, so a parameter-intrinsic watermark is needed.
method: WoE biases the vocabulary of specific experts in MoE models, shifting watermark embedding into model parameters, allowing detection without access to the adversary's deployment.
result: Achieves high true positive rates (90.1% average at 1% false positive) across eight MoE models while preserving utility, and remains detectable under fine-tuning, extraction, and paraphrasing.
conclusion: WoE provides a robust black-box provenance mechanism for MoE LLMs, forcing adversaries into a trade-off between evading detection and maintaining output quality.

title: A Multi-Month Study Of Git Commit Signing
authors: Abubakar Sadiq Shittu, John Sadik, Scott Ruoti
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Git commit signing, introduced in 2012, is one mechanism for establishing commit provenance in software supply chains, yet developer-controlled adoption remains rare and developers' experiences using it are understudied. To examine this experience, we conducted a three-month study with senior undergraduate and graduate computer science students (n = 22), whom we treat as proxies for junior developers. Participants configured commit signing independently, used it across four coursework projects, extended it to a second device, examined an external repository containing anomalous commits, and answered security-reasoning prompts. We found that while almost all participants successfully signed every commit and rated routine signing positively, many faced friction during setup, multi-device configuration, and repository verification. Despite signing all semester, they struggled to spot anomalous commits during verification, with over a quarter finding none. Additionally, nearly half expressed at least one misconception regarding signing guarantees or key management. Without isolating whether these difficulties stemmed from tooling, education, or understanding, we conclude that making signing easier is not enough to ensure effective security use. Rather, secure adoption also requires tools and education that support signature verification against authorized identities, interpretation of missing signatures and unknown keys, and correct reasoning about key-lifecycle operations.
tldr: A user study on Git commit signing reveals that developers face friction in setup and verification, and lack security reasoning despite successful signing.
motivation: To study developers' experiences with Git commit signing, which is underused despite its importance in software supply chains.
method: A three-month study with 22 computer science students, where they configured signing, used it in projects, extended to multiple devices, and answered security questions.
result: Most participants signed successfully but struggled with verification and had misconceptions.
conclusion: Making signing easier is not enough; tools and education must support verification and key lifecycle reasoning.

title: Safe To Resume? Breaking Execution Continuity Of Agent Execution Via Rollback
authors: Guanlong Wu, Dahui Li, Ke Jiang, Jianyu Niu, Cong Wang, Yinqian Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are moving toward persistent, stateful execution across various applications, accumulating execution state and external effects that are costly to reconstruct after failures. Checkpoint and rollback (C/R) are becoming essential for recovery, yet their security implications remain largely unexplored. Correct rollback does not imply secure recovery: a faithfully restored checkpoint may resume an execution whose states, assumptions, and external effects never coexisted in any valid history. In this paper, we present the first systematic security study of checkpoint and rollback in existing agent systems. By examining representative agent C/R systems, we characterize the design space of existing C/R mechanisms and develop a general execution model that captures their recovery boundaries and state dependencies. From this model, we identify five fundamental failure modes spanning incomplete or inconsistent internal state, stale external dependencies, nondeterministic replay, and unrecorded external effects. We further demonstrate their security impact through three end-to-end attacks on Hermes, Cline, and LangGraph, enabling malware-verification bypass, unauthorized mail forwarding, and double payment. To systematically study these failures in practice, we develop a multi-agent analysis pipeline that reconstructs execution semantics, identifies violations of the five failure conditions, and validates them through actual rollback. Across five representative frameworks, our evaluation shows that these failures recur across heterogeneous C/R designs and stem from a common gap between the state restored by a checkpoint and the dependencies required for secure continuation.
tldr: This paper presents the first systematic security study of checkpoint and rollback mechanisms in AI agents, identifying five failure modes and demonstrating real-world attacks.
motivation: AI agents are becoming persistent and stateful, relying on checkpoint/rollback (C/R) for recovery, but the security implications of these mechanisms are unexplored.
method: The authors characterize the design space of existing C/R systems, develop a general execution model capturing recovery boundaries and state dependencies, and build a multi-agent analysis pipeline to reconstruct execution semantics and identify violations.
result: They identify five fundamental failure modes and demonstrate three end-to-end attacks on Hermes, Cline, and LangGraph, showing impacts like malware-verification bypass, unauthorized mail forwarding, and double payment.
conclusion: The failures recur across heterogeneous C/R designs due to a gap between the restored checkpoint state and the dependencies required for secure continuation, highlighting a common security gap in agent systems.

title: Context Or Digits? Balancing Memorability And Efficiency In Virtual Reality Authentication
authors: Yuxuan Huang, Qiao Jin, Tongyu Nie, Victoria Interrante, Evan Suma Rosenberg
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Adaptive Direction-Based Authentication (ADBA), a knowledge-based authentication method for Virtual Reality that decouples users' needs temporally by enforcing password creation based on virtual environment context while supporting both context- and digit-based entries during authentication. This design prioritizes memorability for new passwords and offers both efficient and memorable options to support users' evolving needs. We conducted a remote longitudinal study with 66 participants comparing ADBA against 6-digit PINs over 2-3 weeks. The results demonstrated that ADBA achieved superior memorability and lower perceived task load. Interestingly, no participant chose to enter via digits in the study, yet they still perceived ADBA to be highly efficiency despite longer objective entry times. ADBA also provided security benefits through randomly-generated digit representations, though some degree of password homogeneity was observed in specific virtual environments. Our findings suggest that ADBA offers solid advantages to the traditional PINs, and successfully addresses the tradeoffs between efficiency, memorability, and security under the usage scenarios considered in the study.
tldr: 本文提出一种基于虚拟环境上下文的虚拟现实认证方法（ADBA），在记忆性与效率之间取得平衡。
motivation: 传统PIN码难以记忆，而现有VR认证可能在效率或安全性上存在不足，需要更好的平衡方案。
method: 通过远程纵向研究（66名参与者，2-3周）比较ADBA与6位PIN，ADBA允许基于上下文的方向输入和可选的数字输入。
result: ADBA在记忆性和感知任务负担上优于PIN，但客观输入时间更长，且所有参与者未选择数字输入；同时存在密码同质化问题。
conclusion: ADBA在安全性和可用性方面具有优势，但仍需解决密码多样性等安全问题。

title: JITterFlip: Uncovering Fault Attack Surfaces In JIT-Compiled Llm Serving
authors: Tairui Wang, Zhi Zhang, Yansong Gao, Xin Zhang, Qingni Shen, Zhonghai Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs are widely deployed through cloud-hosted inference services, where Just-in-Time (JIT) compilation is used to reduce recurring framework and GPU-launch overhead. JIT serving introduces a host-side control plane that selects compiled artifacts and orchestrates their execution on the GPU. Meanwhile, the shared cloud setting has motivated a growing body of bit-flip attacks (BFAs) against LLM/DNN inference. Most existing BFAs target model parameters or weights and require model-specific knowledge. A smaller body of work reduces this dependency by faulting executable code, yet still corrupts code that directly implements model computation, limiting their attack effect to inference depletion. We present JITterFlip, the first BFA targeting the host-side JIT serving control plane of GPU-based LLM inference. By faulting CPU-resident serving decisions rather than model computation, JITterFlip enables both gibberish output generation and a correct-output sponge attack. To identify exploitable targets in a large JIT compiler stack, JITterFlip develops a decision-guided fault-vulnerable code analysis. Across four text and multimodal LLM workloads, the identified vulnerable code faults exhibit cross-model transferability, produce gibberish outputs with PPL ratios of [MATH] to [MATH], and demonstrate correct-output sponge attacks with latency amplification of [MATH] to [MATH]. JITterFlip also bypasses recent BFA defenses for LLMs while retaining both attack effects. Last, we demonstrate end-to-end Rowhammer attacks across four LLMs: a single bit flip in CPU-resident branch code propagates across the CPU-GPU boundary to disrupt GPU-executed inference without direct access to GPU memory, reaching up to [MATH] PPL amplification or [MATH] latency amplification while preserving the exact generated output.
tldr: JITterFlip is a bit-flip attack targeting the host-side JIT serving control plane of GPU-based LLM inference, achieving gibberish output and latency amplification without direct GPU memory access.
motivation: Existing bit-flip attacks on LLMs target model parameters or executable code, limiting impact to inference depletion; JITterFlip aims to broaden attack effects by faulting the JIT compilation control plane.
method: The paper develops a decision-guided fault-vulnerable code analysis to identify exploitable targets in the JIT compiler stack and performs bit-flip attacks on CPU-resident branch code to influence GPU-executed inference.
result: Across four LLMs, JITterFlip achieves significant PPL amplification (gibberish) and latency amplification (sponge attack), bypasses existing BFA defenses, and demonstrates end-to-end Rowhammer attacks.
conclusion: JITterFlip reveals a new vulnerability surface in JIT-compiled LLM serving, showing that faulting the control plane can produce serious security impacts while evading current protections.

title: Building The Truman Show: A TrustZone-Based Framework For Lightweight Out-of-band Kernel Security Monitoring
authors: Zhenling Duan, Pan Dong, Renshuang Jiang, Xiaoxiang Fang, Bao Li
abstract: ArXiv:2608.29758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing number of vulnerabilities in operating systems, together with sophisticated kernel-level threats (e.g., rootkits), has weakened the effectiveness of traditional in-kernel protection mechanisms. Since these defenses operate at the same privilege level as the kernel, they share the same attack surface and can be bypassed once the kernel is compromised. Isolation-based security approaches provide stronger protection by separating security logic from the kernel, but strict isolation often introduces semantic gaps that limit system visibility and hinder timely threat detection. In this paper, we present LOOM, a lightweight out-of-band operating system monitoring architecture built on ARM TrustZone. By leveraging TrustZone's hardware-enforced isolation, LOOM establishes a tamper-resistant monitoring environment independent of the kernel. To bridge the semantic gap, we design a lightweight semantic reconstruction mechanism in the Secure World. It selectively captures the states and behavioral patterns of critical kernel objects, such as process control blocks and kernel modules. Additionally, LOOM introduces a dual-stage hazard prevention mechanism that combines atomic memory protection with an interrupt-driven adaptive agent to detect and mitigate kernel rootkit activities. An address translation cache is further incorporated to optimize repeated address access and reduce monitoring overhead. Overall, we develop a multi-layered collaborative architecture with platform, functional, and auxiliary layers for secure and efficient kernel monitoring. A prototype of LOOM has been implemented on the Phytium D2000 platform. Experimental results indicate that LOOM incurs negligible overhead while maintaining a strong monitoring capability. Furthermore, a security capability analysis based on CVE cases demonstrates that LOOM can detect and mitigate various kernel attacks.
tldr: This paper presents LOOM, a TrustZone-based framework for lightweight out-of-band kernel security monitoring to detect and mitigate kernel-level threats like rootkits.
motivation: Traditional in-kernel protection mechanisms share the same attack surface as the kernel and can be bypassed; isolation-based approaches have semantic gaps that limit visibility.
method: LOOM leverages ARM TrustZone's hardware-enforced isolation to create a tamper-resistant monitoring environment, uses a semantic reconstruction mechanism to capture kernel object states, and includes a dual-stage hazard prevention mechanism with atomic memory protection and an interrupt-driven adaptive agent, plus an address translation cache for performance.
result: Prototype implemented on Phytium D2000; negligible overhead while maintaining strong monitoring capability, and can detect various kernel attacks based on CVE cases.
conclusion: LOOM provides a secure and efficient out-of-band kernel monitoring architecture, effectively bridging the semantic gap and mitigating kernel threats.
